authors: Bali, Turan G.; Kelly, Bryan T.; Mörke, Mathis; Rahman, Jamil
title: Machine Forecast Disagreement
publication: The Review of Financial Studies (2026); DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhag042
research_question: How is disagreement among machine-learning return forecasts related to future stock returns?
methodology: Represents heterogeneous investors using different machine-learning model specifications; measures disagreement as the dispersion in return forecasts.
main_relevance_to_our_project: Closest reference: disagreement across machine-learning model specifications is already studied, so disagreement itself is not our contribution.
difference_from_our_project: Studies the relation between disagreement and future stock returns. We do not replicate that return-level test; we study whether disagreement modifies the reliability of a common ML signal at comparable signal levels.

title: What Does Machine Forecast Disagreement Measure?
research_question: What does machine forecast disagreement measure?
methodology: Allows investors to consider multiple forecasting specifications and decomposes total machine forecast dispersion into disagreement across investors and model uncertainty within investors.
main_relevance_to_our_project: Related decomposition of machine forecast dispersion; relevant to our secondary H3 comparison of between-family disagreement and within-family estimation uncertainty.
difference_from_our_project: Its decomposition is across and within investors. Ours compares structurally different model families (Elastic Net, Random Forest, LightGBM, MLP) and, within a fixed family, month-cluster bootstrap replicas intended to capture estimation uncertainty. The two decompositions are related but not identical; our H3 uses this distinction to test whether structural model disagreement and estimation uncertainty contain distinct information about forecast reliability. Our primary question is whether cross-model disagreement identifies variation in the reliability of a common cross-sectional signal, conditional on the signal's level and strength and on observable risk proxies.

title: Confident Risk Premiums and Investments Using Machine Learning Uncertainties
publication: The Review of Financial Studies 39(5), May 2026, pp. 1463-1505; DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhaf087
research_question: How can uncertainty around stock risk-premium forecasts from linear and machine-learning models be quantified, and is it economically relevant?
methodology: Constructs ex-ante confidence intervals around stock risk-premium forecasts from linear and machine-learning models.
main_relevance_to_our_project: Shows that forecast uncertainty can be economically relevant.
difference_from_our_project: Uses model-specific confidence intervals. We use cross-model disagreement and focus on reliability conditional on the ensemble signal level.

authors: Gu, Shihao; Kelly, Bryan; Xiu, Dacheng
title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
publication: The Review of Financial Studies 33(5), 2020, pp. 2223-2273; DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhaa009
research_question: Machine-learning prediction of cross-sectional equity returns.
methodology: Heterogeneous machine-learning model families with strict out-of-sample prediction.
main_relevance_to_our_project: Foundational reference for machine-learning prediction of cross-sectional equity returns; context for heterogeneous model families and strict out-of-sample prediction.
difference_from_our_project: Background methodology, not the novelty of our project. We take ML return prediction as given and study the reliability of the resulting ensemble signal.

authors: Chen, Minghui; Hanauer, Matthias X.; Kalsbach, Tobias
title: Design Choices, Machine Learning, and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
publication: SSRN Working Paper (last revised 15 June 2026); DOI 10.2139/ssrn.5031755
research_question: How sensitive are machine-learning return-prediction results to modeling and design choices?
methodology: Systematic study of more than 1,000 machine-learning specifications.
main_relevance_to_our_project: Documents substantial sensitivity of return-prediction results to modeling and design choices; motivates our strict pre-specification of target, model families, universe and evaluation design.
difference_from_our_project: Studies sensitivity across many specifications. We pre-specify one design and use disagreement among a fixed set of model families as a stock-level uncertainty measure.
